newsitem.title: GERMANY: Report clears Germany's top woman politician.
newsitem.headline: Report clears Germany's top woman politician.

text.p: Germany's embattled parliamentary speaker Rita Suessmuth, who faced calls to resign over charges she misused official aircraft, was exonerated of any wrongdoing by a parliamentary investigation on Wednesday.

But the head of the German taxpayers association, Karl Heinz Daeke, immediately criticised the investigation because he said it should have been carried out by an independent investigator rather than Suessmuth's deputy, Hans-Ulrich Klose.

Klose said Suessmuth had not violated existing rules on the use of military aircraft when she took a total of 12 trips to Switzerland between 1993 and mid-1996 with Bundeswehr aircraft. Suessmuth's daughter lives in Zurich.
Suessmuth, a member of Chancellor Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), denied any charges of wrongdoing and said she used the military aircraft because of her busy schedule.
"It is strange that Mrs. Suessmuth asked her deputy to examine the matter," Daeke said. "Because he himself can also use the aircraft, doubts arise about the independence of this inquiry."
The Handelsblatt business daily reported Kohl plans to clamp down on the use of military aircraft by politicians.
"The whole matter has given politics a bad name," Kohl said, according to the newspaper.
